published_or_official_implementation_cla.current_behavior: Argus planner_verdict_was_persisted scans events.jsonl* and returns a boolean. LifeSupervisor._retry_pending_planner_verdict uses False as permission to call _emit(event) again before acknowledging the outbox.

supervisor_authority.fact: The retry path assigns persisted = planner_verdict_was_persisted(...); if not persisted it calls _emit(event). This makes the boolean absence result operational re-emission authority.

facts: event_log_paths enumerates retained generation pathnames and iter_call_events opens those pathnames later.
Rotation renames .1 to the next numeric generation and live to .1 under the writer's events.lock.
The current writer uses POSIX fcntl.flock when fcntl is available; on Windows fcntl is None, so this event writer currently has no cross-process event lock.
Argus already implements exclusive_file_lock using portalocker.LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB with retry.
Default timeout is 30 seconds, after which it raises TimeoutError rather than waiting indefinitely.

official_artifact_support.declared_dependency: Argus pyproject.toml declares portalocker>=3 with no win32/pywin32 extra.
official_artifact_support.ci_boundary: The portable macOS/Windows matrix includes tests/core/test_file_lock.py but does not include an event-log portability module. The workflow explicitly notes cross-process locking as a portability boundary.

platform_documentation_facts: On POSIX, portalocker defaults to fcntl.flock, so it can interoperate with Argus's existing flock convention if every participant uses the same lock file/primitive.
On Windows, MsvcrtLocker is the default and exclusive locks work with bare portalocker, without pywin32.
Windows shared locking delegates to Win32Locker and requires the optional win32/pywin32 extra; Argus does not declare that extra.
A blocking msvcrt lock itself gives up after about ten seconds, while portalocker.Lock-style retry machinery can implement a longer timeout.
portalocker_primary_support.scope_correction: The worker's proposed correctness-first Windows exclusive reader is supported by the dependency surface. A direct shared-lock port would silently add an undeclared pywin32 requirement.

auditor_reproduction.method: Independent source-shaped transcription of the public scan; Argus was not imported.
results: A target-bearing row containing invalid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError out of the current scan rather than producing persistence evidence.
A malformed JSON row containing the exact delivery_id is skipped and the current scan returns False, although target absence is not proved.
A well-formed target row returns True as expected.
auditor_reproduction.logical_extension_from_source: Any OSError opening/reading a selected generation is also skipped and can still lead to False. Therefore current False conflates proved absence with at least some scan failures/unverifiable target-bearing content.

scope_corrections.finding: The structural defect is that False can authorize re-emission without proof of absence. Whether that produces a durable duplicate depends on the event sink, exact corruption/rollover interleaving and downstream deduplication behavior.
scope_corrections.implication: No production duplicate rate or observed incident is established here.

scope_corrections.finding: Argus's reusable exclusive_file_lock has a 30-second timeout, while the current POSIX event writer uses blocking flock with no equivalent bounded timeout.
scope_corrections.implication: Naively swapping the helper into canonical event authority would introduce a new failure mode under prolonged contention; an explicit event-specific wait contract must be tested.

scope_corrections.finding: Typed UNKNOWN handles unreadable/corrupt evidence but does not by itself eliminate pathname-generation TOCTOU during rollover.
scope_corrections.implication: ABSENT remains safe only if the selected generation ranges are captured under a stable event-lock/snapshot boundary and all selected bytes are scanned successfully.

independent_replication.scope: No third-party protocol-matched Argus fault-injection study or production incident report was established in this audit.

missing_dependencies_or_config.for_proposed_fix: A complete fix needs an explicit event-lock wait/timeout contract, stable-generation snapshot representation, typed evidence API, Supervisor branch semantics and portable Windows regression coverage.

o_specific_adaptation.finding: This is an Argus implementation boundary only. No O/O_FEED/O-state path was read or tested, and no inference about O retry semantics is made.

bottom_line: The worker's central diagnosis is reproducible and source-tight: current planner-verdict persistence is a two-valued query used as retry authority even though some read/corruption states do not prove absence. A target-specific tri-state evidence API is therefore a justified repair direction. The portalocker reuse proposal is also source-supported, but only with an explicit platform/wait contract: bare portalocker gives Windows exclusive locking without pywin32, whereas shared Windows locks require the undeclared win32 extra, and Argus's existing helper times out after 30 seconds. The repair itself and stable-snapshot integration remain unimplemented/unreproduced; no production duplicate incident is claimed.
